For students interested in statistics, data science, or AI, Georgia State University offers an appealing combination: mathematical training, researchers working on substantive problems, and an urban setting where those problems are close at hand. Here are a few reasons to consider GSU when choosing your next place to study.

# Build a foundation, then choose an application

The Department of Mathematics and Statistics offers an **M.S. in Applied Statistics** and a **Ph.D. in Mathematics and Statistics**, alongside mathematics programs and new machine learning and data science concentrations. This creates routes for students interested in statistical methodology, applications, or the interface between statistics and computation. Explore the [department's programs](https://mathstat.gsu.edu/) and compare the [M.S.](https://cas.gsu.edu/program/applied-statistics-ms/) and [Ph.D.](https://cas.gsu.edu/program/mathematics-and-statistics-phd/) curricula with your goals.

# Find collaborators beyond one department

A statistical question can begin with a brain image, an infectious-disease outbreak, an insurance loss, or a student's learning record. At GSU, related expertise spans mathematics and statistics, public health, computer science, business, education, and neuroscience. The university's [research hubs](https://cas.gsu.edu/research/hubs/) and [applied biostatistics and epidemiologic methodology community](https://publichealth.gsu.edu/research-outreach/applied-biostatistics-and-epidemiologic-methodology/) illustrate these connections. My [GSU statistics and related faculty directory](/resources/gsu_statistics_faculty/) is a starting point for finding people whose questions match yours.

# Learn in Atlanta

GSU's location puts students in a city with a substantial public-health community. The School of Public Health highlights opportunities involving the CDC, government agencies, community organizations, and the private sector. For a statistics student, that setting can help connect methods to decisions about health and society. Explore [Population Health Sciences](https://publichealth.gsu.edu/departments-centers/phs/) and the [conference and seminar directory](/resources/conferences_seminars/) for ways to engage with the wider research community.

# Have tools to turn an idea into a study

Simulation studies, large datasets, and machine learning often require more than a laptop. GSU's [ARCTIC](https://arctic.gsu.edu/) provides research computing infrastructure and support; the library's [Research Data Services](https://library.gsu.edu/get-help/data-services/) offers help with data analysis, visualization, and research workflows. My [research computing guide](/resources/gsu_computing/) explains how to get started.

# Look for the right research and funding fit

The department offers competitive graduate lab, teaching, and research assistantships, with additional fellowship routes for eligible doctoral students. Read the [financial support page](https://mathstat.gsu.edu/financial-support/) and ask the graduate director about the terms of a specific offer, including duties, duration, tuition coverage, fees, and summer support.

Before applying, identify two or three potential advisors, read some of their recent work, and write down a research question you would like to explore. A good match between your interests, the available mentorship, and the program's training is a strong reason to choose GSU.

# Notes

Written for prospective students interested in statistics and related fields; official sources checked September 26, 2026. Program requirements, funding, access to facilities, and available projects can change. The linked program and faculty pages provide the current details; nearby organizations and research centers do not imply guaranteed placements or advising arrangements.
